title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC1LA_1RA0LD_1LC0LE_0LF0RA_---1RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC1LA_1RA0LD_1LC0LE_0LF0RA_---1RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a counter: every sweep adds one to a binary-like counter made of odd runs, and the head reaches the left end of the tape only when the counter overflows. Lean proves that a halt can only happen there (in state E). The eight overflows so far came in state D and bounced; the last (step 506,587,790,058) rebuilt the counter about 8·105 cells wide, so the next one is astronomically far away.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: A halt can only happen at the left end
claims.text: A closed tape language from windows of 4 cells covers the run from blank tape; in it the halting transition F0 can only fire with blank tape to the left of the head. So the machine halts iff F reads a 0 with only blank tape to its left (it can only get there as E0 → 0LF).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,625 cells have been visited and 18,342 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: 10<sup>16</sup> steps, eight overflows, no halt
claims.text: An exact run-length simulator (c/tok.c; it agrees with tools/c/tmrun.c at step 10,000,208,949) runs 1016 steps (5.8·107 visits of the right end). The head reaches the left end only at steps 3, 28, 91, 309, 450, 1,252, 7,545 and 506,587,790,058, each time in state D, which bounces.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).

claims.title: A binary counter of odd runs
claims.text: Between visits of the right end the head rewrites the odd runs next to the unit block: (1,3)→(5) every other visit, (3,3)→(7) every 4th, (3,1,5)→(7,3) every 8th, and so on, halving: a binary counter of the visits. Its width stays fixed between overflows (123 cells from step 10<sup>4</sup> to 5·10<sup>11</sup>).

claims.title: The next overflow is ~2<sup>10<sup>5</sup></sup> visits away
claims.text: The eighth overflow turned the 410,921 units into a new counter region of about 8·10<sup>5</sup> cells. The carry depth grew about 7 cells per doubling of the visits in the old counter, so the next overflow, the next chance to halt, needs on the order of 2<sup>10<sup>5</sup></sup> visits.

claims.title: The epoch after step 7,545
claims.text: Between the overflows at steps 7,545 and 5·1011 the tape is a fixed prefix, a reservoir (1,3)^k of run pairs made by the overflow, an active counter region that eats into the reservoir (k = 14, 10, 5, 4, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0 at visits 56, 26..213) and then grows one long run (length 21..33 at visits 212..216), and the units. The numeral system of the active region is not decoded.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: it depends on the state in which the head arrives at the left end at some overflow, which needs the counter's encoding.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LF1LD_0RE0LC_---1LB_1RB1RC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is an odometer: every trip of its head adds one to a counter written with runs of ones, and only when the counter rolls over does the head reach the one place where it could stop. It has rolled over eight times without stopping; the next roll-over is unimaginably far away.

facts.text: The only place a halt can happen (proved).
The last at step 506,587,790,058; each bounced.
No halt in an exact run-length simulation.
Sweeps until the next overflow, the next chance to halt.

sections.heading: An odometer made of runs
html: Write the tape as the lengths of its runs of 1s (separated by single 0s); u is a run of length 1. The tape is a short prefix, a counter region of short odd runs, and a long block of units that grows by one every time the head reaches the right end:

<svg viewBox="0 0 560 44" role="img" aria-label="prefix, counter, unit block" style="width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:11px var(--mono);"><text x="120" y="23" text-anchor="end" fill="var(--muted)">tape</text><rect x="126.0" y="8" width="59.4" height="22" rx="3" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><text x="155.7" y="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">prefix</text><rect x="187.4" y="8" width="120.9" height="22" rx="3" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><text x="247.9" y="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">counter: odd runs</text><rect x="310.3" y="8" width="243.7" height="22" rx="3" fill="var(--heur-bg)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><text x="432.1" y="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">u u u u u u u u ...</text></svg>

On each trip the head walks left over the units, changes the counter a little at its right edge, and walks back. The changes are carries: (1, 3) → (5) happens every other trip, (3, 3) → (7) every 4th, (3, 1, 5) → (7, 3) every 8th, and so on, each kind half as often as the one before. That is exactly how the digits of a binary counter change when you add 1, so the region counts the trips.

sections.heading: Only when the counter rolls over
html: The machine stops only when state F reads a 0, and Lean proves (with a closed tape language from windows of 4 cells) that this can only happen at the very left end of the tape, after state E steps off it. The head gets there only when a carry runs through the whole counter: an overflow, like an odometer going from 999,999 to 1,000,000.

That has happened eight times, the last three at steps 1,252, 7,545 and 506,587,790,058. Each time the head arrived in state D, which writes a 1 and turns back, so the run went on. The last overflow also turned the 410,921 units into a new counter region about 820,000 cells wide.

Filling a counter that wide takes on the order of 2100,000 trips, so the next chance to stop is far beyond any computer. Whether the head would then arrive in D (no halt) or E (halt) depends on how the counter's digits are written, which is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,625 cells (10 left of the start, 26,854 right), with a density of 1s of 0.501.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A binary-like counter of odd runs counts the sweeps; only when it overflows does the head reach the left end, the only place a halt is possible (proved in Lean); the eight overflows so far (the last at step 5.07·10<sup>11</sup>) bounced, and the last one widened the counter to ~8·10<sup>5</sup> cells, putting the next chance to halt ~2<sup>10<sup>5</sup></sup> sweeps away.
family: counter that overflows at the left end
